faq_heading: Questions sales teams ask about booking meetings on LinkedIn

faqs.q: How many messages does it take to book one meeting?
faqs.a: It varies by offer, market and list quality, so no honest single number exists. Track the chain instead: invites sent, acceptances, real replies and booked calls, and improve the weakest step first.

faqs.q: Should I ask for the meeting in the first message?
faqs.a: Usually not. A first note that asks for a call from a stranger tends to feel pushy. Connect with a short, relevant note, then ask once there is a reply or clear interest.

faqs.q: How many follow-ups are too many?
faqs.a: Two or three, spaced several days apart, is a sensible limit. Stop at once when someone replies or says no.

faqs.q: Can an AI agent book the meetings for me?
faqs.a: It can handle the finding, messaging, follow-up and sorting of replies. A person should confirm the meeting and run the call, because trust is built in the conversation.

faqs.q: Is it safe to automate LinkedIn outreach?
faqs.a: There is some account risk, since LinkedIn restricts automated activity that breaks its rules. Modest, personal, human-paced volume is the best way to reduce it.
